summary: The checkpoint proof copies the store by cloning it where the filesystem can (APFS, btrfs/XFS reflink) instead of VACUUM INTO, holding its read only while the files clone, and commits its preparation on the scratch copy, so it needs far less free disk and no minutes-long read

replay.detail: No replay, backfill, stored data or transcript change. The proof compares the same digests and answers; it runs on a scratch copy that is deleted afterwards.

schema.detail: Published schema, operations and contract digest are unchanged.

rules.detail: No claim, checkpoint, retention or authority rule change. Checkpoint plans and proofs are identical.

compatibility.detail: Nothing a client or peer sees changes. Hosts whose filesystem cannot clone (ext4) still copy in full.

downtime.detail: Ordinary rolling deployment; no data conversion or extra startup work.

recovery.detail: No recovery, durable payload or initialization changes.
